title: Short Stuff: Lake Erie's Rights
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss Toledo, Ohio's Lake Erie Bill of Rights and the broader Rights of Nature movement. They cover the Global Alliance for the Rights of Nature, the legal idea of giving ecosystems legal standing, Ecuador's 2008 constitution and Bolivia's 2010 Universal Declaration of the Rights of Mother Earth. They describe the August 2014 Toledo water crisis caused by a cyanobacteria algae bloom, Markie Miller and the Toledo Wins for Safe Water group, the petition and vote, the roughly $300,000 opposing campaign, and a lawsuit by an agricultural company that led Judge Jack Survey to strike the law down. The episode closes with a brief look at Rights of Nature efforts in other places. The opening banter includes Josh's Toledo roots and a joke about a key to the city.

segments.title: Key to the city banter and Toledo intro
segments.summary: Josh, a Toledo native, jokes with Chuck about a never-received key to the city and introduces the episode's topic of Toledo's Rights of Nature effort.

segments.title: Rights of Nature concept and early national examples
segments.summary: The hosts explain the Global Alliance for the Rights of Nature and the idea that ecosystems can have legal rights, comparing it to corporate personhood. They note Ecuador's 2008 constitution and Bolivia's 2010 Universal Declaration of the Rights of Mother Earth.

segments.title: August 2014 Toledo water crisis
segments.summary: A cyanobacteria algae bloom in Lake Erie contaminated Toledo's water intake, leaving residents without safe tap water for three days. The hosts attribute the bloom to agricultural fertilizer runoff.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Short sponsor break with a host-read promo for a podcast, including a mention of Marky Miller as a great Toledoan.

segments.title: Markie Miller and Toledo Wins for Safe Water
segments.summary: Markie Miller, a Toledo resident, pushed local officials for answers after the water crisis. She and others formed Toledo Wins for Safe Water, which led to the Lake Erie Bill of Rights. The hosts also recall Lake Erie's earlier pollution and later recovery.

segments.title: Ballot vote, industry opposition, and court ruling
segments.summary: Supporters collected double the signatures needed to put the bill on the ballot. It passed, but about twelve hours later an agricultural company sued. Judge Jack Survit struck it down as too vague and as overreaching across state lines. The hosts close by mentioning Rights of Nature efforts in Hawaii, Florida and Washington State.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh wrap up, noting the article source and a plug for the iHeartRadio app.
